objective.statement: Keep one persistent full J-Code TUI attachable from SSH and a secure browser terminal while retaining one long-lived J-Code daemon.
objective.measure: SSH and the loopback browser terminal attach to one named tmux TUI, the browser listener is restricted to 127.0.0.1, and exactly one J-Code serve process remains active.

need.statement: Mikael needs to operate the full J-Code TUI across disconnects from SSH and a browser without spawning additional agent daemons or exposing a public shell.
stakeholders: Mikael operating J-Code remotely from SSH or a browser through an SSH tunnel.
need.baseline: The J-Code daemon and SSH path are live, but jcode connect is line-oriented, no shared tmux TUI exists, ttyd is absent, and nothing listens on port 7681.
need.consequence_of_no_action: Remote reconnects either create independent TUI frontends or remain line-only, and no browser terminal can reach J-Code.
alternatives_considered: Use independent jcode --resume TUI clients instead of sharing the exact screen
Enable the J-Code WebSocket gateway even though it has no browser TUI frontend
Expose ttyd publicly with basic authentication

purpose: Keep one persistent full J-Code TUI attachable from SSH and a secure browser terminal while retaining one long-lived J-Code daemon.
consumer: Mikael operating J-Code remotely from SSH or a browser through an SSH tunnel.
contract: Home Manager provides a jcode-tui command backed by one named tmux session and a user WebTTY service bound only to 127.0.0.1; both attach to the existing J-Code daemon and do not expose a public shell.
failure_boundary: The WebTTY must remain loopback-only and must not alter or stop jcode-server.service. If the WebTTY, tmux attachment, or single-daemon invariant fails, keep SSH and the daemon available and do not expose the browser endpoint on a non-loopback address.

evidence.description: Home Manager contract tests prove the wrapper and loopback-only service declaration; live probes prove one tmux TUI, an HTTP endpoint on 127.0.0.1:7681, and one J-Code daemon.

falsifier.claim: SSH and browser access share one persistent full TUI without exposing a public shell or creating another daemon.

executable_check.description: Run the repository check and live listener/process probes; any non-loopback ttyd listener, missing tmux TUI, or second jcode serve process falsifies the claim.

non_goals: Implement a native browser frontend for the J-Code WebSocket gateway
Change J-Code provider or model failover
invariants: jcode-server.service remains the only long-lived J-Code daemon
The WebTTY listener binds only to 127.0.0.1
SSH remains key-only and independently usable
Browser disconnects do not terminate the tmux-hosted TUI
No secret is embedded in the Nix module or command line

assumptions.statement: The Nixpkgs ttyd package is available for this host.
assumptions.falsifier: nix eval or build cannot resolve nixpkgs#ttyd.

assumptions.statement: The full J-Code TUI can run as a client of the existing daemon inside tmux.
assumptions.falsifier: A tmux-launched plain jcode process fails to register as a client of the existing server.

assumptions.statement: A loopback-only ttyd listener reached through SSH forwarding does not create a public shell endpoint.
assumptions.falsifier: ss reports ttyd listening on any non-loopback address.

plane_constraints: Home Manager owns the wrapper and user services; network exposure remains loopback-only.
